question.problem:
The matrix $T$ is given below. Let ${t}_{1}$, ${t}_{2}$, and ${t}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $T.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{t}_{1},{t}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(T).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${t}_{2}={x}_{1}{t}_{1}+{x}_{3}{t}_{3}.$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $T$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(T)$ is $\{{t}_{1},{t}_{2}\}.$

Therefore, we conclude that $\text{{}{t}_{1},{t}_{3}\text{}}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(T).$
